whyThisShow: This is the show the Fillmore East run is remembered by, and the Dark Star at its center is the reason. One listener who was there described "the places they went, and the changes they went through during that time, were unlike anything I had ever seen or heard before, including the Allmans earlier that night or the Dead themselves earlier that year". Another reviewer described "an insanely inventive Dark Star that drops down to silence before charging back up into a monster Feeling Groovy jam and then Bob drives the band through the most high energy Other One I've ever heard". The sequence closes with Pigpen steering Lovelight back to earth, and that same reviewer noted the band "managed to make the connection" after the cosmic territory they had just covered. Dark Star, The Other One, and Lovelight were officially released on Dick's Picks Vol. 4, with the Archive source carrying a fuller picture of the night.
listenFor: The Dark Star is the main event — track the moment it drops to near-silence, which one attendee recalled so vividly: "at the points where the music is quiet, almost silent, the audience was also so quiet you could have heard a pin drop". When the Dead emerge from that stillness they do not go to St. Stephen as the crowd expected — one witness recalled that "when we all expected they would go into St. Stephen from DS, they went into The Other One, which drew a collective gasp from the audience". One reviewer singled out the continuous arc of the Dark Star through The Other One into Lovelight as "one of the best continuous jams ever". The recording itself is soundboard and one listener found it "STRAIGHT SOUND BOARD, STEREO MIX, AND SOUNDS ALBUM READY".
context: February 1970 was one of the Dead's densest runs at the Fillmore East, and this Friday-night late show came the night before another legendary performance on the 14th — both nights were eventually compiled for Dick's Picks Vol. 4. The Archive source (gd70-02-13.early-late.sbd.cotsman.18114.sbeok.shnf) is a soundboard and carries more of the full night than the official release, including an acoustic set, some of which one reviewer noted "can be heard on Bears' Choice". The Allman Brothers opened that night, and at least one attendee arrived already floored by what the Allmans had done, only to find himself reconsidering everything once the Dead took the stage.
funFact: One eyewitness recalled that "it was dawn when the concert let out and the sidewalk outside the Fillmore was filled with people, like me, who couldn't believe what we had just witnessed".
headline: Dark Star into The Other One, Fillmore East, February '70.
